newsitem.title: GERMANY: VEW - higher energy earnings boost profits.
newsitem.headline: VEW - higher energy earnings boost profits.

text.p: Germany electricity group VEW AG said on Monday that it expected a moderate rise in net profits in full year 1996.

The group said that better earnings in its energy division in the current year had led to an improvement in overall group net profit in the first nine months of the year to 129 million, an increase of nine percent.
"We expect to show a profit for 1996 which will allow us to give a good return on share capital as well as allowing the necessary strengthening of reserves," VEW said in a letter to shareholders.
VEW Energie had counteracted a drop in sales in the nine-month period with a lowering of costs across its divisions, VEW said.

The group said its 1996 earnings would allow it to pay an "appropriate" dividend, an expression which VEW has on previous occasions used when it planned to keep the dividend unchanged. In 1995 VEW paid out a dividend of nine marks.

Earnings in the group's east German subsidiary MEAG were boosted principally by increased demand for electricity after the long winter, while contributions from its Harpen services unit were slightly lower.
The group said that earnings at its Edelhoff waste disposal unit were still unsatisfactory.
